answer.rationale: Switching primary outright (per memory_c2) would meet the 18% mandate on price alone, but with the line at 94% of committed volume, zero buffer, and 14 days to expiry, a full cutover to a vendor whose record I have only from a consolidated summary is an unacceptable delivery risk — and memory_c2 says nothing about quality, capacity, or ramp performance under shortage conditions. Renewing the incumbent fails the finance mandate and they have refused to reopen price, and deferring is impossible since the contract does not auto-renew. The one decision that fits is qualifying the low-cost vendor as a second source on a small, guarded volume split: it begins capturing unit-cost savings toward the mandate, removes the single point of failure before the constrained period (consistent with memory_c3), and builds the performance evidence needed for a larger shift next cycle. I am verifying memory_c2 and memory_c3 because the intended action leans directly on both, and both are consolidated summaries whose archived originals may contain caveats (volume levels, component scope, duration) that change how much volume I would initially allocate. Confidence is moderate pending those pulls.
